title: Fish and Vegetables without Carrots, Broccoli, Dark‑Green Leafy Greens

content.title: About
content.content: A combination of tender fish (such as salmon, cod, or hake) with a variety of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens and potatoes, creates a light, nutrient‑dense dish rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals. Preparing it without soy sauce makes it suitable for those avoiding soy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fish is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart and brain health.
Vegetables like zucchini, bell pepper, tomatoes, and cauliflower provide antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.
Excluding potatoes lowers the dish’s glycemic index, making it more suitable for blood‑sugar control.
Steaming preserves most of the vitamins and minerals in both fish and vegetables.
Fish‑and‑vegetable dishes are staples in Mediterranean diets, known for their health benefits.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fish supplies complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: These polyunsaturated fats reduce inflammation and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish and vegetables contain B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish provides iodine, selenium, magnesium, and potassium, which aid thyroid function, immunity, and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Omitting potatoes and starchy vegetables makes the meal suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury or other toxins; choosing smaller species and reputable sources is advisable.

items.title: Excess sodium
items.content: If the dish is heavily salted or uses ready‑made seasonings, sodium intake can become too high, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Improper storage
items.content: Fresh fish‑vegetable dishes spoil quickly at room temperature; keep refrigerated and consume within 1‑2 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The dish can be served hot, baked, or steamed. Cut fish into bite‑size pieces and vegetables into large cubes, then bake together with a drizzle of olive oil and herbs (such as thyme or rosemary). Serve with lemon wedges or a light yogurt‑based sauce without soy.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in the oven or a steamer before serving. Do not freeze fish together with vegetables for long‑term storage, as texture may deteriorate.
